topic.name: Defining Double Integrals Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

question.text:
Let $R = [0,4]\times [2,6]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Calculate the double integral \[ \displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}A. \] where $f$ is a function such that $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=4$ for all partition $P$ of $R,$ and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Now, since $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=4,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} L(f,P) = U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n 4 \, \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] %&= 4 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &= 4 \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j \bigg)\\[5pt] &= 4(4-0)(6-2)\\[5pt] &= 4\cdot 4\cdot 4\\[5pt] &= 64. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\[ L(f,P) = 64 \leq \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A \leq 64 = U(f,P) \] which implies that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = 64. \]

example.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

question.text:
Let $R = [1,4]\times [1,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Calculate the double integral \[ \displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}A, \] where $f$ is a function such that $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=-2$ for all partitions $P$ of $R,$ and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Now, since $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=-2,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} L(f,P) = U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (-2) \, \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] %&= -2 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &= -2 \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j \bigg)\\[5pt] &= -2(4-1)(4-1)\\[5pt] &= -2\cdot 3\cdot 3\\[5pt] &= -18. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\[ L(f,P) = -18 \leq \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A \leq -18 = U(f,P) \] which implies that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = -18. \]

example.title: Calculating a Double Integral Using Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

question.text:
Let $R = [-1,2]\times [-4,-1]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 3x-8y+6.$ Further, let

\[ \displaystyle I = \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm dA \]

be the unique number such that over all rectangular partitions $P$ of $R,$ we have $ L(f,P)\:\leq I \:\leq U(f,P), $ where $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P)$ are the corresponding lower and upper Riemann sums, and

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\fbox{$\phantom{AAAAA}$} \: \Delta x_i \Delta y_j\,. \]

What expression is missing from the double summation above?
question.choice5: None of the options is correct
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

We need to compute $U(f,P).$

Notice that for all subregions $R_{ij},$ we have that

  • $f(x,y) = 3x-8y+6$ increases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 3x-8y+6$ decreases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible $x$ and the smallest possible $y.$ This is the value at the bottom right corner of each subregion. Therefore,

\[ M_{ij} = f(x_i, y_{j-1}) = 3x_i-8y_{j-1}+6 \]

and the upper Riemann sum is given by

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n ({\color{blue}{3x_i-8y_{j-1}+6}})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \]

So, the missing expression is $3x_i-8y_{j-1}+6.$

\[ \displaystyle I = \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm dA \]

be the unique number such that over all rectangular partitions $P$ of $R,$ we have $ L(f,P)\:\leq I \:\leq U(f,P), $ where $L(f,P)$ and $U(f,P)$ are the corresponding lower and upper Riemann sums, and

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\fbox{$\phantom{AAAAA}$} \: \Delta x_i \Delta y_j\,. \]

What expression is missing from the double summation above?
question.choice5: None of the options is correct

For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Notice that for all subregions $R_{ij},$ we have that

  • $f(x,y) = 10+y-3x$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 10+y-3x$ increases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the maximum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible $x$ and the largest possible $y.$ This is the value at the top left corner of each subregion. Therefore,

\[ M_{ij} = f(x_{i-1}, y_j) = 10+y_j-3x_{i-1} \]

and the upper Riemann sum is given by

\[ U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n ({\color{blue}{10+y_j-3x_{i-1}}})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \]

So, the missing expression is $10+y_j-3x_{i-1}.$

question.text:
Let $R = [-1,3]\times [2,5]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Calculate the double integral \[ \displaystyle\iint\limits_R f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}A, \] where $f$ is a function such that $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=-3$ for all partitions $P$ of $R,$ and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ respectively in each subregion $R_{ij}.$
question.explanation:
For a function $f(x,y),$ the double integral of $f$ over a rectangular region $R$ is the unique number $I$ (if it exists) such that

\[ L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P), \]

over all partitions $P$ of $R,$ where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

\begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j\\[5pt] U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n M_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*}

and $m_{ij}$ and $M_{ij}$ are the minimum and maximum values of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

Now, since $m_{ij}=M_{ij}=-3,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} L(f,P) = U(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (-3) \, \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] %&= -3 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \\[5pt] &= -3 \bigg( \sum_{i=1}^m \Delta x_i \bigg) \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j \bigg)\\[5pt] &= -3(3-(-1))(5-2)\\[5pt] &= -3\cdot 4\cdot 3\\[5pt] &= -36. \end{align*}

Finally, we obtain

\[ L(f,P) = -36 \leq \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A \leq -36 = U(f,P) \] which implies that \[ \iint\limits_R f(x,y)\,\textrm d A = -36. \]
